content.title: Coulomb’s Law
content.summary: Magnitude of electrostatic force between two point charges.
content.explanation: Magnitude of electrostatic force between two point charges.
content.when_to_use: Use for point charges in vacuum or a uniform medium.
conditions: Charges are treated as point charges.

example.question: If both charges are doubled, how does F change?

common_mistakes: Forgetting inverse-square dependence.

content.title: Electric Field Definition
content.summary: Electric field is force per unit positive test charge.
content.explanation: Electric field is force per unit positive test charge.
content.when_to_use: Use to relate force and field.

example.question: A 2 N force acts on a 1 C test charge.

common_mistakes: Confusing field with force.

content.title: Capacitance
content.summary: Capacitance is charge stored per unit potential difference.
content.explanation: Capacitance is charge stored per unit potential difference.
conditions: Capacitance is a property of geometry and medium.

example.question: A capacitor stores 2 C at 4 V.

common_mistakes: Confusing capacitance with charge.

content.title: Energy Stored in Capacitor
content.summary: Energy stored in the electric field of a capacitor.
content.explanation: Energy stored in the electric field of a capacitor.
content.when_to_use: Choose the form matching known quantities.
conditions: The capacitor must be charged as specified.
common_mistakes: Using CV² without one-half.

content.title: Ohm’s Law
content.summary: For an ohmic conductor at constant physical conditions, voltage is proportional to current.
content.explanation: For an ohmic conductor at constant physical conditions, voltage is proportional to current.
conditions: Temperature and physical conditions remain constant.
common_mistakes: Applying blindly to non-ohmic devices.

content.title: Magnetic Force on Moving Charge
content.summary: Force on a charge moving in a magnetic field.
content.explanation: Force on a charge moving in a magnetic field.
content.when_to_use: Use for a moving charge in a magnetic field.
conditions: Force is zero for parallel motion.

example.question: When is force maximum?
example.answer: When velocity is perpendicular to B.

common_mistakes: Ignoring angle.

content.title: Faraday’s Law of Induction
content.summary: Induced emf is related to the rate of change of magnetic flux.
content.explanation: Induced emf is related to the rate of change of magnetic flux.

example.question: What does the negative sign indicate?
example.solution: It gives the direction opposing the change.

common_mistakes: Dropping the physical meaning of minus sign.

content.title: RMS Value of AC
content.summary: RMS values give equivalent heating effect for sinusoidal AC.
content.explanation: RMS values give equivalent heating effect for sinusoidal AC.
content.when_to_use: Use for sinusoidal alternating current or voltage.
common_mistakes: Confusing peak and RMS values.

content.title: Lens Formula
content.summary: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance using Cartesian sign convention.
content.explanation: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance using Cartesian sign convention.
common_mistakes: Mixing lens and mirror conventions.

content.title: Einstein Photoelectric Equation
content.summary: Photon energy is used for work function and maximum photoelectron kinetic energy.
content.explanation: Photon energy is used for work function and maximum photoelectron kinetic energy.
conditions: Frequency must exceed threshold for emission.

example.question: If hν=5 eV and φ=2 eV, find Kmax.

common_mistakes: Confusing intensity with photon energy.

content.title: Radioactive Decay Law
content.summary: Number of undecayed nuclei decreases exponentially with time.
content.explanation: Number of undecayed nuclei decreases exponentially with time.
conditions: Decay is statistical and unaffected by ordinary physical conditions.
common_mistakes: Confusing decay constant with half-life.

content.title: Photoelectric Effect Graph
content.summary: Stopping potential or maximum kinetic energy versus frequency.
content.y_axis: maximum kinetic energy or stopping potential
content.relationship: Above threshold frequency, maximum kinetic energy increases linearly with frequency.
interpretation: Threshold frequency is the x-intercept for suitable graph form.
Intensity mainly changes photocurrent, not maximum kinetic energy.
important_points: Slope is related to Planck constant in appropriate units.
